The root cause was in the refactored `format_exc_info` in `stackprinter/formatting.py`: it (1) dropped all support for chained exceptions (`__cause__`/`__context__`), (2) crashed on `None` values (`issubclass(None, ...)` in the suppression check and `etype.__name__`/`evalue.text` in `format_exception_message`), and (3) mis-assembled the message — the `'auto'` summary triggered on `len(frames) > 1` instead of the documented ">50 lines" threshold, so a "Traceback (most recent call last):" summary was wrongly prepended to nearly every traceback, pushing the exception message out of place. The fix: early-return `format_exception_message` for `None` etype/evalue/tb (yielding "NoneType: None" and "TypeError: None" as the stdlib does), guard the SyntaxError branch against `evalue=None`, derive the type name from `type(evalue)` when `etype is None`, make `add_summary='auto'` trigger only when the rendered stack exceeds 50 lines, restore chained-exception formatting by recursively prepending the cause/context with the standard "The above exception was the direct cause..." / "During handling..." headers (summaries only for the outermost exception under 'auto'), and use the previously-unused `traceback` import to render suppressed exception types (e.g. KeyboardInterrupt) as a standard Python traceback, while tolerating `suppressed_exceptions=None`. All 7 existing tests pass, plus extensive extra checks for chains, reverse/colored styles, suppression, and None inputs.
